setting.name: Montana Drones
setting.tagline: 1930s artefact hunters racing rivals and Nazis for lost relics
setting.blurb: It is 1936 and the world is in a period of transition. Every major power is trying to vacuum up as many ancient artefacts and relics as they can lay their hands on, so wary global powers work through freelance agents to protect and recover these powerful symbols. At the request of Army Intelligence, Dr Abigail Elizabeth Joens, Professor of History at Halcyon Hall (better known as Montana Drones) and her team travel the globe in search of lost or hidden artefacts, exploring dangerous sites and racing hostile enemy agents. Striking locations, exciting chases, dangerous enemies and monotonous classroom lectures await!
rules: Any Role from the ACE! core rules works for artefact hunters; the book adds four New Occupations (Botanist, Double-Agent, Socialite, Witch).

Witch grants a Power stat and the Evil Eye: an opposed roll against a target's Smarts steals 1 Karma from the target (you still gain 1 from Mooks and Extras with none to lose); not usable on other Heroes, and only once per Mook or Extra.
Botanists identify any plant (including plant-derived substances such as poisons) without a roll, and plant creatures won't attack them.
A Double-Agent's disguise always works when wearing an enemy uniform.
A Socialite's name is always on the guest list.

1936 technology: television is rare and the size of a dressing table, telephones are dial type but a call costs more than a telegram, no jet engines and no computers at all — research must be done the old-fashioned way.
Cost uses the core rules purchase table (p. 16) as a reference; for prices more reflective of the 1930s, divide the Amount column by 10.

Purchase difficulties: up to $10 no roll (telegram, second-hand revolver or bullwhip); up to $1,000 TN 10 (phone call, pistol, motorbike); up to $10,000 TN 20 (television set, international flight); up to $100,000 TN 30 (house, luxury car); up to $1,000,000 TN 40 (own ship or airplane).
The corselet of Mégês grants its wearer +2 Defence.
The Cutty-Sark lets its wearer use the witch's Evil Eye power and gives a Power score of 3 (Eric Freeman when wearing it).
A witch can spend Karma stolen with the Evil Eye to fuel other magical effects (see Using Magic, ACE! core p. 22).

Pregenerated Heroes (Montana Drones, Lou Doble, Jonah Henry Jr, Johnnie Cobbler) are a free download from awfullycheerfulengine.com; with original Heroes, one should be a globetrotting treasure hunter based at Halcyon Hall and one is Eric Freeman's rival.

roles.name: Botanist
roles.ability: You love plants. You can identify any plant without a roll, including substances made from plants (we're looking at you, poisons). Also, plant creatures won't attack you. Everyone else is fair game, though.

roles.name: Double-Agent
roles.ability: You're a bit like a spy, only you enjoy dressing up in the uniform of the bad guys and gals. If you put on an enemy uniform to fool your foes, your disguise always works.

roles.name: Socialite
roles.ability: You are one of the social elite, or perhaps your fame or notoriety means you get invited to all the top parties. Either way, your name is always on the guest list.

roles.name: Witch
roles.ability: You made a deal with the devil. It cost you your soul, but you gained some supernatural gifts. You have a Power stat. You can also use your Evil Eye to steal Karma from others: make an opposed roll against a target's Smarts. If it succeeds, the target loses 1 Karma point and you gain 1. You still gain 1 Karma from Mooks and Extras even if they don't have any to lose. You can't use your Evil Eye on other Heroes, and you can only use it on each Mook or Extra once.

gear.name: Telegram
gear.description: Send a telegram. Up to $10; cheaper than placing a telephone call in 1936.

gear.name: Second-hand Revolver
gear.description: A worn but serviceable revolver. Up to $10.

gear.name: Bullwhip
gear.description: The artefact hunter's signature tool. Up to $10.

gear.name: Telephone Call
gear.description: Place a telephone call on the old dial type telephone. Up to $1,000.

gear.name: Television Set
gear.description: The size of a dressing table and almost as rare as hen's teeth, but just beginning to become practical. Up to $10,000.

gear.name: International Flight Ticket
gear.description: Purchase a ticket for an international flight. Up to $10,000.

gear.name: Luxury Car
gear.description: Buy a luxury car. Up to $100,000.

gear.name: Ship
gear.description: Buy your own ship. Up to $1,000,000.

gear.name: Airplane
gear.description: Buy your own airplane. Up to $1,000,000.

extras.name: Desert Nomad
notes: Thirty or more surround the Heroes at Petra; if the Heroes fight, every Hero suffers 3 damage each round until everyone is unconscious.
extras.description: Mubtasim desert nomads of Petra, guardians of the Soldier Tomb, armed with bows and rifles and led by Eric Freeman.

extras.name: Eric Freeman
notes: Eric gains +2 to his Defence when he's wearing the corselet of Mégês.
Eric can use the witch's Evil Eye power when he's wearing the Cutty-sark (see p. 20).
Eric's Power score is 3 when wearing the Cutty-sark.
extras.description: Eccentric tomb raider and unrepentant rival in artefact hunting; fellow former student of history at Oxford University with a smugly superior attitude. Slipperier than an eel.

extras.name: Giant Frog

attacks.name: Sticky Tongue
attacks.note: 15-foot range, restrains target and pulls them to the frog, needs Brawn 10 check to escape

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.note: only on targets caught by its sticky tongue

extras.description: A frog the size of a rhinoceros, its vocal sac expanding and contracting rhythmically before its ginormous tongue flicks out.

extras.name: Vinetacles

attacks.name: Lash
attacks.note: 20-foot range, needs Brawn 20 check to escape

notes: Once reduced to zero Health, a vinetacle gently slithers to the ground and releases its hold.
Vinetacles don't squeeze further once they have a victim; they lift the target and hold them aloft, waiting.
Fire axes reduce the Defence of each vinetacle by 2.
extras.description: Vines that have become tentacles, pulsating and gyrating like the limbs of some giant amorphous beast, gripping Halcyon Hall.

extras.name: Kufooloo
notes: Award the Heroes a Karma point once the creature is defeated.
The vinetacles throughout the school turn to mush as soon as the creature dies.
extras.description: A half-formed creature: eight stunted tentacles propel a stocky torso with half-formed wings jutting from its back, and a broad rubbery head with tentacles growing from its jawline.

extras.name: Nazi Agent
extras.description: Enemy agents of Operation: Scymitar, brought in by Eric Freeman to help recover the Cutty-Sark.

extras.name: Hell Hound
notes: A 'friend' called in by the witches Blair and Coira; ravages any it can get its jowls on and slinks away into the darkness once the enemy agents are dealt with.

extras.name: Witch

attacks.name: Evil Eye
attacks.note: Opposed roll against a target's Smarts. If it succeeds, the target loses 1 Karma point, and the witch gains it.

notes: The witch can use Karma stolen with the Evil Eye to fuel other magical effects, see "Using Magic", p. 22 of ACE!
extras.description: The old crones Blair and Coira, who live in a crumbling cottage outside Ayr and hold the Cutty-Sark.
